text:
The Capitals were down 2-0 in the first period, and Alex Tuch got them out of the hole twice. He scored on a backhand that our numbers gave a 2% chance of going in, then won it in overtime on a snap shot at 3:42 of the extra period. That made it a 4-3 comeback over Buffalo. Tuch, drafted 18th overall by the Wild in 2014, finished with two goals.

The Sabres got their early lead from Jack Quinn and Josh Doan, both on modest chances, and Washington spent the rest of the night taking the game back. Dylan Strome tied it early in the second and put Washington ahead late in the period, finishing with two goals and an assist. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, favored Washington 4.03 to 2.34, and the Capitals took the second period 1.90 to 0.96. Our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that Washington wins, put the Capitals at 76%. Jordan Kyrou added two assists, and Jakob Chychrun had two more over 25 minutes of ice time.

The Sabres didn't go quietly. Noah Ostlund's wrist shot tied it at 3-3 early in the third, and Buffalo's 24 giveaways to Washington's 15 hint at how loose the game got. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 30 of 34 shots and finished almost exactly on expected, while Charlie Lindgren allowed three on 21 shots. Neither power play scored, with Washington 0 for 3 and Buffalo 0 for 2. We have no streaks or standings to add, but Washington leaves with a come-from-behind win and Buffalo with a point's worth of regret.
